bug_description.normalized: In the exact staged OpenSC checkout `61cd7fcdb2fdc9214b431abb631b202314dcc32f`, `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` treats the 158-byte witness as a fake smart-card transcript and reaches synthetic CAC certificate loading. `cac_read_binary()` invokes `cac_cac1_get_certificate(card, &val, &val_len)` with local `val == NULL`, so `cac_cac1_get_certificate()` selects its internal 4096-byte stack buffer `buf` as the certificate destination and carries `next_len` across APDU reads. On continuation responses, the vulnerable code recomputes `next_len = MIN(left, apdu.sw2)` before the loop increment `left -= len, out_ptr += len` runs, so a later iteration can reuse a stale `len` that is larger than the now-reduced `left`. When a later terminating response takes the `apdu.sw1 != 0x63 || apdu.sw2 < 1` branch, `left -= len` unsigned-wraps the remaining-space counter. The subsequent `r = size - left` becomes 4240 even though `buf` is only `CAC_MAX_SIZE == 4096`, and the guarded `memcpy(*out_buf, buf, r)` overreads 144 bytes past the end of the stack buffer. Local commit `b75c002cfb1fd61cd20ec938ff4937d7b1a94278` fixes the bug by updating `left` and `out_ptr` before recalculating `len`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled libFuzzer input as the fake reader transcript later consumed by the reader callbacks on the CAC certificate-read path.
source.value_from: The staged 158-byte `poc` (sha256 `14ff0392f0b6563f2ef45920f48828b90f66f99a36b80c3c955332186018a90d`) passed to `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; `fuzz_add_reader()` stores that raw buffer and size in `reader->drv_data`.
source.note: Later `fuzz_get_chunk()` and `fuzz_reader_transmit()` calls slice fake APDU responses from this saved transcript state.

sink.description: ASan-correlated sink. Because `cac_read_binary()` passed `val == NULL`, line 107 allocates `*out_buf` and line 113 copies from helper-owned stack `buf`. After `left` wraps, `r` becomes 4240, so `memcpy(*out_buf, buf, r)` reads 4240 bytes from `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`, overrunning the 4096-byte source buffer by 144 bytes.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4240` at `src/libopensc/card-cac1.c:113` and names `buf` at line 68 as the overread stack object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The loop carries `next_len` forward from the current `left` before `left -= len, out_ptr += len` runs. After prior iterations shrink `left`, the next iteration can still reuse the larger stale `len`.
root_cause.note: Local commit `b75c002cfb1fd61cd20ec938ff4937d7b1a94278` removes `next_len`, moves `left -= len; out_ptr += len;` into the loop body before recalculating `len`, and thereby prevents this stale-length carry.

tainted_value_origin.description: The unscored libFuzzer entry hands the witness buffer to the project helper that creates the fake reader transcript state.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the harness boundary, not the scored source.

parser_admitted.description: Synthetic CAC initialization reaches certificate loading, so the fake reader transcript has been admitted far enough to invoke `cac_cac1_get_certificate()`.
parser_admitted.note: The saved crash stack includes this call site.

evidence_limitations: Reviewer feedback required separating the continuation-path and terminating-path receives. Because `fuzz_get_chunk()` advances `data->Data` by only `sizeof *chunk_size` and the saved artifacts do not log reader-callback ordinals or exact APDU status bytes, this GT models them as distinct source-level iterations rather than exact numbered `fuzz_reader_transmit()` calls. `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation.

ARVO metadata reports `a3ee8cefc8057ae9199edbafc96643b4f225654e` / `3c87ffaa021ea53a84a2fe3977ecea945b4cc5b3`, and the staged `patch.diff` is commit `7a1e42e1352201127d1a97b6cb5f41e48cace0f5` (`fixed compiler warning`) in the fuzz harness. Those artifacts do not explain the reproduced `card-cac1.c` overread; the actual source-side fix used here is local commit `b75c002cfb1fd61cd20ec938ff4937d7b1a94278`.

coarse_trace.summary: The project stores the libFuzzer input as the fake reader transcript that later reader callbacks interpret as APDU responses.
Synthetic CAC initialization requests a certificate file and enters the CAC certificate-read path.
The CAC driver initializes local `val = NULL` and calls `cac_cac1_get_certificate(&val, &val_len)`, selecting the helper-owned output-buffer path.
The helper uses its fixed 4096-byte stack buffer `buf` and carries `next_len` across continuation responses.
Attacker-controlled transcript chunks become APDU status words: an earlier continuation response stores a stale `next_len`, and a later terminating response takes the break path.
The stale `len` exceeds the reduced `left`, `left -= len` wraps, `r` becomes 4240, the null-output guard allocates `*out_buf`, and `memcpy(*out_buf, buf, r)` overreads the stack buffer.

fine_trace.note: Stores the staged 158-byte witness as the fake reader transcript. All later reader callbacks slice ATR and APDU bytes from this saved `data->Data` / `data->Size` state.

The transcript is admitted far enough that synthetic CAC initialization requests the certificate file from the card. Through `sc_pkcs15_read_file()` -> `sc_read_binary()` -> `card->ops->read_binary`, this request reaches the CAC driver's `cac_read_binary()` on the saved crash path.

The CAC driver does not pass its caller-supplied `buf` or `count` into the certificate helper. Instead it initializes local `val` to NULL and passes `&val`, so `cac_cac1_get_certificate()` enters with `*out_buf == NULL`; that state selects the helper's stack `buf` path and later satisfies line 107's `if (*out_buf == NULL)` guard.

Because step 2 passed `&val` with `val == NULL`, the helper takes the null-output branch, sets `size = left = sizeof(buf) == 4096`, points `out_ptr` at stack `buf`, and seeds the first request length with 100 bytes. This establishes both the fixed source extent and the stack object later overread by `memcpy`.

fine_trace.var: len, next_len, out_ptr, left, apdu.resp, apdu.le, apdu.resplen
fine_trace.note: On the earlier continuation iteration that seeds the stale carry, the loop copies the current `next_len` into `len`, points the APDU response buffer at the current tail of `buf`, and advertises the current remaining capacity in `apdu.resplen`.

For that continuation-path receive, `fuzz_get_chunk()` consumes two transcript header bytes, materializes `*chunk_size`, advances `data->Data`, and returns `*chunk` pointing at the attacker-controlled bytes that `fuzz_reader_transmit()` will interpret.

This earlier callback turns the current chunk's last two bytes into APDU status words. On the crash-consistent path those bytes keep the certificate loop on its continuation path, so the guard at line 95 is false and execution falls through to line 101.

Root cause. Because the continuation response left the line 95 guard false, line 101 stores the next request length from the current pre-increment `left`. The subsequent loop increment can shrink `left` before this stored `next_len` is reused.

fine_trace.code: for (; left > 0; left -= len, out_ptr += len) {
fine_trace.note: At the end of that continuation iteration, the loop increment executes `left -= len, out_ptr += len`. This makes the remaining space smaller while step 7 has already preserved the older larger request size in `next_len`.

fine_trace.var: len, next_len, out_ptr, left, apdu.le, apdu.resplen
fine_trace.note: On a later terminating iteration, the loop reuses the carried `next_len` as the new `len` after step 8 has already reduced `left`. `apdu.le` therefore keeps the stale larger request size while `apdu.resplen` exposes the smaller remaining buffer tail. From the saved `READ of size 4240` with `size == 4096`, this terminating iteration necessarily has `len = left + 144`.
For the later terminating receive, `fuzz_get_chunk()` advances the transcript cursor again and returns the next attacker-controlled chunk that supplies the status bytes for this iteration.

This later callback turns its chunk's last two bytes into APDU status words. On the crash-consistent path those bytes satisfy the break condition, so line 95 takes the terminating branch instead of recalculating `next_len` again.

With step 9's stale `len` now larger than the reduced `left`, the terminating branch executes `left -= len; break;`. Because `left` and `len` are `size_t`, subtracting `left + 144` from `left` wraps the remaining-space counter into a huge unsigned value.
Using the wrapped `left`, the function computes the final copy length from the fixed 4096-byte buffer extent. The observed underflow by 144 bytes makes `r == 4240`.

Because step 2 left `*out_buf` null, the line 107 guard is true after the underflow. The helper allocates `r` bytes for the destination buffer and keeps stack `buf` as the source of the upcoming copy.

Sink. With step 14's allocated `*out_buf`, `memcpy` reads 4240 bytes from stack `buf[4096]`, so the final 144 bytes come from the redzone and adjacent `apdu` area. ASan reports this exact call as `stack-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 4240` and names `buf` at line 68 as the overread object.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: ARVO metadata's reported fix commit and staged `patch.diff` point to fuzz-harness changes, but local commit `b75c002cfb1fd61cd20ec938ff4937d7b1a94278` changes `src/libopensc/card-cac1.c` exactly on this chain by moving the `left` / `out_ptr` updates ahead of recalculating `len`. That source change prevents the stale-length carry and removes the overread described here.

poc.trigger: The staged 158-byte PoC is consumed as a fake reader transcript. On the reproduced path, synthetic CAC certificate reading reaches `cac_cac1_get_certificate()`, a continuation response stores `next_len` from pre-decrement `left`, and a later terminating response causes `left -= len` to wrap so `memcpy(*out_buf, buf, r)` overreads 4240 bytes from the 4096-byte stack buffer.

format.contract: Exactly the staged 158-byte witness stored in `poc` (sha256 `14ff0392f0b6563f2ef45920f48828b90f66f99a36b80c3c955332186018a90d`). The file is interpreted as the fake reader transcript used for ATR setup and later APDU responses. On the observed CAC certificate-read path, later transcript bytes make `cac_cac1_get_certificate()` receive one or more continuation responses that set `next_len = MIN(left, apdu.sw2)` before `left` is decremented, and a later terminating response arrives after `left` has shrunk below the carried `len`. That witnessed response pattern makes `left -= len` wrap by 144 bytes, so `r = size - left` becomes 4240 and `memcpy(*out_buf, buf, r)` overreads 144 bytes past `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class beyond this exact witness and observed response sequence.
